subject: Parameters passed to kde2d from stat_density2d

messages.author: 55d1e12d2e4acfaf
messages.subject: Parameters passed to kde2d from stat_density2d
parts:
If you look at the code for stat_density2d, the argument n=100 is
passed internally to kde2d. This affects the amount of smoothing and
is not the same as the default. Because of the way the code is
written, the user cannot pass a different value to override n=100.

I wonder if there is a workaround to this limitation and whether or
not it might be changed in a subsequent release.

messages.author: 55d1e12d2e4acfaf
messages.subject: Re: Parameters passed to kde2d from stat_density2d
parts:
I don't actually want to change it at this point as I am just learning
ggplot. As I was working through the examples, however, I noticed that
ggplot gave me a different picture than the one I made myself directly
using kde2d. I misinterpreted the way n affects the results, but
nonetheless, ggplot doesn't give the default behavior of kde2d. I
think that is fine as long as it is called out. But I don't think, as
a matter of principle, that you should hard code parameters of a
secondary function without allowing the user access to change them. So
I would argue that if you think that n=100 is a better default choice,
which I do agree with, you should use it as a direct argument to
stat_density2d. Other arguments, for which you don't have a strong
opinion, can be continued to be passed via the ellipsis.
